chunks: My father (rah) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Aban al-Ahmar from Abu Usamah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Sadaqah at night extinguishes the anger of the Lord.'

key_terms.صَدَقَةَ اللَّیْلِ: Sadaqah at night (charity given during the night)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of giving charity at night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) identifies night-time charity as a specific means of appeasing the Divine, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Sadaqah* as a spiritual remedy for *Ghadab* (divine wrath). This teaching aligns with the broader tradition that night prayers and voluntary acts carry heightened efficacy due to the quietude of the world and the proximity to the Divine Presence.
